evidence: Swap test fails: the frame (white header with a small outline bin glyph and the council name in bold sans, pale grey-green ground, bold sans H1 'Book a slot', outlined day buttons, a grid of bordered time tiles with 'Few left'/'Full' chips, a dark-green rectangular primary 'Next', a bordered info box, a one-line grey footer) would carry a library room booking or a swimming-session booking unchanged with only the words swapped.

Category-guess test fails: a UK council transactional service predicts exactly this (GOV.UK-like single column, one dark green accent, bold sans headings, error summary box with a red border, a large reference number on the confirmation).
Similar-prompt test fails: 'book a slot at a council household waste site in another district' or 'book a bulky-waste collection' would land on the same grid, palette and type.

What is specific is content only: Quarry Road DN4 2XQ, 20-minute slots, the DRC- permit, rubble up to four bags, 'not on the gate's list'. With the name hidden the purpose is readable only from the words, not the design.

unfinished: identity is only the council name in bold body-size sans beside a generic outline bin glyph; nothing of the recycling centre (site, bays, waste streams, the gate) appears visually
no focal point on vehicle or confirm: each is a heading followed by a stack of default-looking fields and full-width checkbox rows
headings differ from body mostly in size and weight within one sans family; no typographic moment anywhere, including the reference on the done page

half-empty layout at 1280 and 1440: forms and slot grid stop at about 710-820 px inside a 1180 px column, leaving the right half empty while the 'Opening days' and 'Your booking' boxes stretch full width with text in their left half
done page at 1280: the page ends at about 715 px and the white footer band stops short, leaving a flat grey band beneath it
an unlabelled block of 'Few left' tiles sits above the 'Morning' heading, out of time order, so the grid reads as unfinished grouping
phone number '01632 960771' and 'DN4 2XQ' wrap across lines in the 375 footer and done card
evidence: / at 1280 light: the first viewport is a heading, a grey sentence, a plain-text step list and four outlined buttons, then the slot grid.
vehicle (van, 1280 light): seven identical white checkbox rows under a bold heading; nothing else to look at.
done at 1280 light: DR-204117 as a bold heading inside a plain white card with an empty right half.

Colour does one job (dark green actions, amber 'Few left'); no imagery, illustration or drawn device. Clean and orderly in both themes, but it reads as a default service-pattern form rather than something made for Dunmore.
